name: Genetic Neurological Muscular Channelopathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Genetic Neurological Muscular Channelopathy

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of muscle weakness or paralysis triggered by exercise, stress, or potassium imbalance
Electromyography (EMG) showing myotonia or abnormal muscle excitability
Identification of pathogenic mutations in voltage-gated ion channel genes (e.g., SCN4A, CACNA1S, KCNJ2)
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Episodes associated with abnormal serum potassium levels (hypokalemia or hyperkalemia)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent muscle weakness episodes with electrophysiological evidence and pathogenic genetic mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is critical for definitive diagnosis; clinical presentation may vary.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paralytic episodes triggered by potassium imbalance
searchTerms: paralysis triggered by low or high potassium

pathognomonic.symptomName: Myotonia characterized by delayed muscle relaxation
Muscle stiffness exacerbated by cold exposure
searchTerms: increased muscle tone with cold exposure

common.symptomName: Muscle cramps during or after physical activity
searchTerms: muscle cramps during or after activity

common.symptomName: Fluctuating serum potassium levels during episodes

occasional.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias associated with channel dysfunction
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems linked to channel defects
cardiac arrhythmias from ion channel issues
abnormal heartbeats due to channel dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Mild ptosis or facial muscle weakness
searchTerms: drooping eyelid or mild face weakness

occasional.symptomName: Muscle hypertrophy in affected muscle groups

searchTerms: shortness of breath from weak breathing muscles
breathing difficulty due to muscle weakness

rare.symptomName: Seizure-like activity secondary to electrolyte imbalance

laboratory: Serum potassium abnormalities during paralytic episodes
Elevated creatine kinase (CK) levels during attacks
imaging: Normal muscle MRI or mild muscle edema during acute episodes
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SCN4A, CACNA1S, or KCNJ2 genes
other: Electromyography demonstrating myotonic discharges or abnormal muscle excitability

distinguishingFeatures: Periodic paralysis without confirmed channel gene mutation
Serum potassium changes but no myotonia
Progressive muscle wasting and multisystem involvement
Characteristic CTG repeat expansions in DMPK gene

redFlags: Sudden onset of respiratory muscle weakness
Progressive permanent muscle weakness outside episodic attacks
